summary: As a pre-trial design, Advanced remains plausible. A solver must connect duplicate identity, persisted financial effects, payer capacity, clearing, ledger recognition, reconciliation and close. Plausible local repairs can remain globally wrong. This does not set final difficulty: the final tier must come from the combined GPT-5.5 x5 plus Claude Opus 4.8 x5 complete-run mean, with every verifier test passing at least once across those 10 trials.

evidence.observation: Broad restart branches make ALREADY_* states look like new execution while finalization can still publish/complete from inconsistent state.
Starter persistence layer does not itself enforce one financial effect, so solver must reason about DB and controller together.
Twelve named scenarios/test cases probe clean, completed rerun, partial internal/external restart, reconciliation hold, eligibility, pending history, and each close prerequisite.
Claude Opus 4.8 x5 plus GPT-5.5 x5 are combined and their mean sets final difficulty.
Across 10 runs, each individual verifier test must pass at least once for the task to be considered solvable.

do_not_change: Do not harden with arbitrary thresholds or unrelated edge cases.
Do not reject or tier the task from either five-run model suite alone.
Do not call 8/10 or 9/10 automatically too easy; those results are Base under current Edition 3 ranges.
next_gate: Empirical combined 10-trial difficulty and trajectory analysis after current Oracle/NOP/LLMaJ pass
